analyzed_vuln.description: Heap buffer overflow is caused by zeroing a JPEG-LS state object through a miscast pointer: `JLSState *state = &((JpegLSDecodeContext*)s)->state;` followed by `memset(state, 0, sizeof(*state));`. Here `s` is actually an `MJpegDecodeContext*` (from mjpeg decoder), not a `JpegLSDecodeContext*`, so `state` points into/just past unrelated heap memory (the codec context allocation seen in ASan), and `memset` writes 5924 bytes out of bounds. Crash occurs at this memset in `ff_jpegls_decode_picture` (called from `ff_mjpeg_decode_sos`).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: In the AMV-target fuzzer path, crafted input drives MJPEG lossless JPEG-LS decode (`s->lossless && s->ls`) so `ff_mjpeg_decode_sos` calls `ff_jpegls_decode_picture(s, predictor, point_transform, ilv)`. Because the function performs an invalid cast from `MJpegDecodeContext*` to `JpegLSDecodeContext*`, any invocation can corrupt heap; the provided PoV reaches it with minimal data and triggers immediate OOB write at state initialization.
